name: Aspect of Immortality AP OLD

items.name: Scythe
items.description: Derived from a farming tool used to mow down long grains and cereals, this weapon has a long wooden shaft with protruding handles, capped with a curved blade set at a right angle.

generalAbilities.name: Death's Grace
generalAbilities.description: The Aspect of Immortality can choose whether or not it counts as undead for effects that affect undead differently. Even if it does not count as undead, the Aspect of Immortality still never counts as a living creature.

generalAbilities.name: Status Sight
generalAbilities.description: The Aspect of Immortality automatically knows the Hit Points, conditions, afflictions, and emotions of all creatures it can see.

savenote: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

defensiveAbilities.name: Aura of Misfortune
defensiveAbilities.description:
20 feet. Living creatures in the aura must roll twice on all d20 rolls and use the lower result.

Effect: Aura of Misfortune

defensiveAbilities.name: Key Weakness
defensiveAbilities.description: Jatembe's history of vanquishing the King of Biting Ants survives in the halcyon legacy of the Magaambya. The Aspect of Immortality has a key weakness to both arcane spells and primal spells.

defensiveAbilities.name: Lurking Death
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger A creature within 100 feet makes a ranged attack or uses an action that has the concentrate, manipulate, or move trait.

Effect The Aspect of Immortality teleports to a square adjacent to the triggering creature and makes a melee Strike against it. If the Strike hits, the Aspect of Immortality disrupts the triggering action.

defensiveAbilities.name: Void Healing
defensiveAbilities.description:
The Aspect of Immortality can choose whether or not it takes vitality damage.

See rules...

A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

offensiveAbilities.name: Death Strike
offensiveAbilities.description: A creature critically hit by any of the Aspect of Immortality's attacks or that critically fails against any of its spells must succeed at a DC 47 Fortitude Saving Throw save or die.

offensiveAbilities.name: Energy Drain
offensiveAbilities.description: When the Aspect of Immortality hits and deals damage with its scythe, it regains 20 Healing Damage Hit Points, and the target must succeed at a DC 43 Fortitude Saving Throw save or become Doomed 1. If the target is already doomed, the doomed value increases by 1 (to a maximum of doomed 3).

offensiveAbilities.name: Final Death
offensiveAbilities.description: A creature killed by the Aspect of Immortality can't be brought back to life by any means short of divine intervention.

offensiveAbilities.name: Infuse Weapon
offensiveAbilities.description: Any scythe gains the agile trait, can't be disarmed, and becomes a +3 Major Striking Keen scythe while the Aspect of Immortality wields it. If the Aspect of Immortality Strikes a creature with a weakness to any specific type of damage, the scythe's damage counts as that type of damage, in addition to slashing.

lv2spells.name: See Invisibility (Constant)
lv2spells.description:
You can see Invisible creatures and objects. They appear to you as translucent shapes, and they are Concealed to you.

Heightened (5th) The spell has a duration of 8 hours.

lv3spells.name: Haste (Constant)
lv3spells.description:
Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the Quickened condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

lv6spells.name: True Seeing (Constant)
lv6spells.description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion or transmutation in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

lv7spells.name: Plane Shift
lv7spells.targets: 1 willing creature, or up to 8 willing creatures joining hands
lv7spells.description: You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must have specific knowledge of the destination plane and use a magic tuning fork created from material from that plane as a focus for the spell. While the tuning forks for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell plane shift, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare tuning forks. The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20x25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Plane shift doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting plane shift again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

lv10spells.name: Finger of Death
lv10spells.description:
You point your finger toward the target and speak a word of slaying. You deal 70 void damage to the target. If the damage from finger of death reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the target dies instantly.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 10.
